metadata.title: Set Up Environment Variables and API Key Management

story.iWant: to securely manage environment variables and API keys
story.soThat: sensitive information is protected and configuration is environment-aware
story.tasks:
- Task 1: Create environment variable files (AC: 1) - Create .env.local with OPENWEATHER_API_KEY placeholder - Create UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL placeholder - Create UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN placeholder - Create .env.example with documented placeholders (no actual values) - Verify .env.local is already in .gitignore (from Story 1.1)
- Task 2: Create environment variable validation utility (AC: 1) - Create lib/env.ts for environment variable validation - Define EnvironmentVariables TypeScript interface - Implement validateEnv() function to check required vars on startup - Export typed env object for use across the app - Add clear error messages for missing variables
- Task 3: Test environment variable access (AC: 1) - Create test API route to verify env var loading - Test accessing OPENWEATHER_API_KEY from API route - Verify environment variables are NOT accessible client-side - Test with missing env vars to validate error handling - Document environment variable setup in README
- Task 4: Document API key acquisition (AC: 1) - Add section to README explaining how to obtain OpenWeather API key - Document Upstash Redis account setup - Provide clear instructions for copying .env.example to .env.local - Add troubleshooting section for common env var issues

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. **Given** the project needs external API integration **When** I configure environment management **Then** a .env.local file is created for local development **And** .env.example file documents required environment variables **And** OpenWeather API key placeholder is defined **And** .env.local is added to .gitignore **And** environment variables are accessible in API routes **And** the app validates required env vars on startup

doc.snippet: API keys stored in .env.local (not committed), .env.local added to .gitignore, .env.example documents required variables (no actual values). Critical security requirement for API key protection.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Foundation & Infrastructure
doc.snippet: Documents Node.js 18+ requirement, system requirements (4GB RAM, 500MB disk), and version constraints. OpenWeather API key placeholder needed in .env.example for Epic 2 readiness.

doc.title: TEST3 - Epic Breakdown
doc.section: Story 1.3: Set Up Environment Variables and API Key Management
doc.snippet: Story acceptance criteria: Create .env.local for local development, .env.example documents required variables, OpenWeather API key placeholder defined, .env.local in .gitignore, env vars accessible in API routes, app validates required env vars on startup.

doc.title: Architecture Document
doc.snippet: OpenWeather One Call API 3.0 for 24-hour hourly forecast with precipitation probability. Free tier provides 1K calls/day. API key configuration required for Epic 2 integration.

doc.title: Architecture Document
doc.snippet: Planned OpenWeather API client with retry logic. Will require OPENWEATHER_API_KEY from environment variables. Story 1.3 sets up the environment infrastructure that Epic 2 will consume.

doc.title: TEST3 - Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: Manual location entry respected (no geolocation tracking), no saved searches or user data persistence, analytics limited to location + timestamp only. Environment variable security supports privacy-first architecture.

Type definitions for process.env and Node.js built-ins.

constraint.rule: Server-side only: Environment variables must NEVER be exposed to client-side code
Variables prefixed with NEXT_PUBLIC_ are client-accessible - AVOID for API keys
.env.local must be in .gitignore (verify from Story 1.1 - already present)
.env.example documents structure but contains NO real values (placeholders only)
Use TypeScript for type-safe environment access - no 'any' types
TypeScript strict mode enabled - all environment code must be strictly typed
Create centralized validation in lib/env.ts (not scattered across codebase)
Fail fast on startup if required variables are missing
Provide helpful error messages directing to .env.example
Allow optional variables for Epic 2 onwards (graceful degradation)
Next.js automatically loads .env.local at startup (no additional configuration needed)
Environment variables are read at build time for static pages
Place .env.local and .env.example in project root (will-it-rain/ directory)
Place env.ts validation utility in lib/ directory alongside utils.ts
Optional test API route should be in app/api/test-env/route.ts if created

interface.name: EnvironmentVariables
interface.notes: Define this interface in lib/env.ts. TypeScript strict mode enforces all fields. Epic 1 treats API keys as optional for initial setup.

interface.name: validateEnv()
interface.notes: Centralized validation function called at application startup. Should check process.env and return typed object.

interface.name: env
interface.notes: Single source of truth for environment variables. Import this throughout the application: import { env } from '@/lib/env'

interface.name: process.env
interface.signature: // Server-side only - automatically populated by Next.js process.env.OPENWEATHER_API_KEY process.env.UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL process.env.UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN process.env.NODE_ENV
interface.notes: Next.js loads .env.local at startup. Access via process.env in API routes and server components only. NOT accessible in client components.

tests.standards:
Epic 1 follows manual validation approach with no automated tests required (per tech spec). Testing focuses on: - Manual verification through development and build commands - TypeScript compilation checks (tsc --noEmit) for type safety - Visual inspection and console logging for environment variable access - Git status checks to verify .env.local is not tracked - Clear error messaging validation when variables are missing
Testing tools: TypeScript compiler, ESLint, Next.js dev/build commands, browser DevTools, git command line.
tests.locations: No dedicated test directories for Epic 1 (foundation only). Testing occurs through: - Command line: npm run dev, npm run build, npm run lint, tsc --noEmit - Browser: localhost:3000 for visual validation - Git: git status to verify .env.local ignored - Optional test API route: will-it-rain/app/api/test-env/route.ts (if created for Task 3)

test.description: Verify .env.local created with all required placeholder variables
test.approach: Check file exists at will-it-rain/.env.local with OPENWEATHER_API_KEY, UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL, UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN placeholders

test.description: Verify .env.example documents all variables with no real values
test.approach: Check file exists at will-it-rain/.env.example with documented placeholders and acquisition instructions

test.description: Verify .env.local is in .gitignore and not tracked by git
test.approach: Run 'git status' after creating .env.local - should NOT appear in untracked files (already covered by .env* wildcard)

test.description: Verify lib/env.ts validation utility exists with TypeScript interface
test.approach: Check will-it-rain/lib/env.ts exports EnvironmentVariables interface, validateEnv() function, and env object

test.description: Verify environment variables accessible in API routes
test.approach: Create test API route that imports { env } from '@/lib/env' and logs values - verify server console shows environment variables

test.description: Verify validation catches missing environment variables with clear error
test.approach: Temporarily remove .env.local, run 'npm run dev' - should show helpful error message directing to .env.example

test.description: Verify environment variables NOT accessible client-side
test.approach: Attempt to access process.env.OPENWEATHER_API_KEY in a client component - should be undefined. Browser DevTools should not show API keys.

test.description: Verify TypeScript compilation passes with strict mode
test.approach: Run 'tsc --noEmit' or 'npm run build' - should complete with no type errors in env.ts

test.description: Verify README documents environment setup clearly
test.approach: Check README includes section on obtaining OpenWeather API key, Upstash setup, and copying .env.example to .env.local

test.description: Verify dev server runs successfully with valid environment variables
test.approach: With .env.local present and valid, run 'npm run dev' - server should start on localhost:3000 without errors
